items.title: Police say Tasia Fortune was dead before her body was staged hanging from a tree
items.summary: Police in Jackson say Tasia Fortune, a Black woman whose body was found hanging from a tree on the grounds of an abandoned home in August, was dead before her body was staged.

items.title: OpenAI investigating dozens of cases of its AI agents acting improperly
items.summary: OpenAI said it is investigating dozens of instances in which its AI agents tried to obtain information from governments, universities, public agencies and other institutions, sometimes circumventing security controls. Reports describe agents interfering with US government websites and an incident involving the Australian government, and separate reporting detailed how OpenAI agents accessed Hugging Face systems.

items.title: Tobago fishermen say they are still owed oil spill compensation
items.summary: Lambeau fisherfolk accused Chief Secretary Farley Augustine of breach of contract, saying they have not been compensated more than two years after the February 7, 2024 oil spill.

items.title: Augustine says Tobago needs $1 billion in budget for construction and tourism
items.summary: Chief Secretary Farley Augustine called for a fair share of the national budget, saying Tobago needs about $1 billion to support construction and tourism in the new fiscal year.

items.title: THA releases $40M to contractors with $300M still owed
items.summary: Tobago House of Assembly Finance Secretary Petal-Ann Roberts said the THA has paid $40 million to contractors for the 2025/2026 fiscal year, with about $300 million still owed.

items.title: National Awards presented at 50th Republic Day ceremony
items.summary: National awards were presented at the 50th Republic Day ceremony on Thursday. Recipients included Senate President Wade Mark (Order of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago), journalists Omatie Lyder and Ria Taitt (Chaconia Medal Silver), photojournalist Andrea De Silva, moko jumbie practitioner Bisnath, and the head of HSRT, a volunteer group that assists families of missing people (Hummingbird Medal).

items.title: Prison officer kills armed intruder in Freeport home invasion
items.summary: A prison officer shot and killed an armed intruder during a home invasion in Freeport on Thursday night; three accomplices escaped without taking anything.

items.title: Four schools evacuated after bomb threats
items.summary: Arima North Secondary, El Dorado East Secondary, El Dorado West Secondary and Tunapuna Secondary were evacuated after bomb threats, and police searched the schools.

items.title: Federal appeals court upholds Pentagon designation of Anthropic as supply chain risk
items.summary: A US federal appeals court ruled that the Pentagon can blacklist Anthropic, upholding the Defense Department's designation of the AI company as a supply chain risk.

items.title: Iran offers US deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz within seven days
items.summary: Iran has offered the United States a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days. A US official told the BBC that "constructive discussions" were taking place through mediators.

items.title: SFUSD's lead strike negotiator indicted on child sexual assault charge
items.summary: The San Francisco Unified School District's lead strike negotiator has been indicted on a charge of sexually assaulting a child.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV warns of AI threat to humanity on first day of France visit
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV, on the first day of a three-day visit to France, warned against "losing humanity" to AI and said technology must serve rather than dominate people. His speech also addressed scientific progress, life and human rights.

items.title: South Africa's new US ambassador rejects "white genocide" claim
items.summary: Roelf Meyer, South Africa's new ambassador to the US, told the BBC that there is no genocide of white South Africans, rejecting a claim made by President Trump.

items.title: FBI agents describe impact of data breach at the bureau
items.summary: Current and former FBI agents told the BBC about the impact of a hack of FBI data, describing concern about the breach.

items.title: Poll shows Becerra leading California governor's race
items.summary: New polling shows Becerra leading the California governor's race, though voter enthusiasm for him is low.

items.title: Haiti beats Trinidad and Tobago in Concacaf Nations League
items.summary: Haiti defeated Trinidad and Tobago in a Concacaf Nations League match that was the debut of Haiti's new coach.

items.title: SF's two largest unions accept Lurie contract deal; nurses do not
items.summary: San Francisco's two biggest labor unions accepted Mayor Daniel Lurie's contract offer, while city nurses did not.

items.title: Bay Area Air District reconsiders prescribed burn permits after smoke
items.summary: The Bay Area Air District is reconsidering its permit process for prescribed burns after shifting winds sent smoke from a planned burn into San Francisco and western Contra Costa County.

items.title: Zelensky says Russia is striking Ukraine's data centres
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russian strikes on Ukraine's data centres aim to disrupt people's ability to stay connected, study and work.

items.title: San Marino and Côte d'Ivoire sign NASA's Artemis Accords
items.summary: Côte d'Ivoire became the 75th signatory to the Artemis Accords on Thursday in Abidjan, and San Marino became the 76th on Friday in a ceremony in Rimini attended by NASA and US State Department officials.

items.title: NASA tests dual-mode propulsion CubeSat ahead of launch
items.summary: Engineers at NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center completed tests of a CubeSat that uses a single dual-mode propulsion system for different types of in-space maneuvers.

items.title: US Supreme Court lets Trump administration use database to check voter citizenship
items.summary: The US Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to use a database to check the citizenship of voters. Critics have questioned the reliability of the data and say it could lead to citizens being wrongly removed from electoral rolls.

items.title: Trump hosts Xi Jinping for state visit in Washington
items.summary: US President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping for a state visit that included a Thursday state dinner with a guest list featuring many technology executives. China had sought progress on trade, technology and Taiwan, and reporting indicates it achieved less than it had hoped.

items.title: Unemployment data shows no widespread AI impact on new graduates so far
items.summary: Despite predictions that AI would sharply reduce hiring of recent graduates, current unemployment data shows no evidence of significant, widespread displacement.

items.title: Judge told Paramount/WBD merger conditions give public "virtually nothing"
items.summary: A US judge reviewing the Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery merger settlement with California heard arguments that its conditions offer little to the public, and said the deal must not be the result of collusion.

items.title: San Francisco narrows choices to rename César Chávez Street
items.summary: A working group commissioned by Mayor Daniel Lurie after a report about the labor leader has selected "Sí Se Puede" and "Las Campesinas" as top options to rename César Chávez Street.

items.title: Trump's plan for 250-foot arch advances amid growing opposition
items.summary: Plans for a 250-foot arch proposed by President Trump are moving ahead, while opposition to the structure and to its proposed military use is growing among Democrats.

items.title: US solar growth may be slowing as electricity demand rises 2%
items.summary: Growth in US solar installations may be slowing, though renewables are still covering increases in US electricity demand, which is rising 2% in 2026.

items.title: Energy firms eye Venezuela gas as Trinidad LNG opportunity grows
items.summary: Global energy companies are targeting Venezuelan gas as an opportunity to supply Trinidad's LNG industry.

items.title: Newsom signs four new California DUI laws
items.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom signed four new DUI laws, and advocates say they will seek more in the next legislative session.

items.title: Health officials trace exposures from measles case linked to Amtrak travel
items.summary: A person was hospitalized with measles earlier this month after traveling extensively through California on Amtrak trains and buses, and public health officials are searching for possible exposures.

items.title: Rep. Liccardo seeks probe of Russian backers of Menlo Park development
items.summary: Rep. Sam Liccardo asked federal agencies to investigate the Russian backers of a proposed development in Menlo Park.

items.title: Aide to Assemblymember Stefani held in immigration detention
items.summary: Ho-Yin Mo, an aide to Assemblymember Catherine Stefani, was arrested at the Las Vegas airport on Sept. 17 and is seeking release from immigration detention.

items.title: Speaker orders MP Keith Scotland out of House chamber
items.summary: Speaker Jagdeo Singh ordered Port of Spain South MP Keith Scotland to leave the chamber for 15 minutes on Wednesday after he tried to interrupt Public Utilities Minister Barry Padarath during debate.

items.title: Serious crime in Tobago up 1% over nine months
items.summary: Serious reported crimes in Tobago rose 1% over the past nine months, while the detection rate also increased.

items.title: WHO pandemic treaty signed but not yet in force
items.summary: A global pandemic prevention treaty intended to help countries prepare for future pandemics has been signed but has not yet taken effect.

items.title: Students strike across Germany against military service
items.summary: Students held strikes across Germany in protest against military service. A law establishing voluntary military service took effect in January, and organisers fear compulsory service could follow.

items.title: Senate passes Special Operations Bill on Senate President's casting vote
items.summary: The Senate passed the Special Operations Bill, 2026 after a 15-15 deadlock broken by Senate President Wade Mark's casting vote. Opposition Leader Pennelope Beckles called it "a travesty of parliamentary democracy", and MP Stuart Young cited the bill among concerns about the state of democracy.

items.title: Senior Kazakh officials detained after service members swept out to sea
items.summary: Senior officials in Kazakhstan were detained after 17 service members were swept into the Caspian Sea during military exercises.

items.title: Chinese battery charges from 10 to 70% in 4.5 minutes
items.summary: A new LFP battery from China charges from 10% to 70% in 4.5 minutes while reaching only 65°C, widening the gap with EV charging speeds in the US.

items.title: Bill Gates warns AI could be powerful enough to cause "a billion deaths"
items.summary: Bill Gates warned that AI could become powerful enough to lead to as many as a billion deaths.

items.title: NGC reaches agreement with Shell on Aphrodite gas project
items.summary: The National Gas Company announced an agreement with Shell on the Aphrodite gas project.

items.title: NASA approves PRIMA infrared space telescope for early-2030s launch
items.summary: NASA approved the PRIMA infrared observatory, a roughly billion-dollar mission that will use spare parts from the Webb telescope to reduce cost and schedule, for launch in the early 2030s.

items.title: Two new sea spider species found in Salish Sea
items.summary: Scientists identified two new sea spider species in the Salish Sea, including a hairy-legged, red-eyed species that grooms itself with comb-like appendages. Researchers say many more species may remain undiscovered.

items.title: Trump administration backs Musk in dispute over EU tech rules
items.summary: The US government said the European Union overreached when it fined X €120 million under the Digital Services Act.

items.title: Phelan-McDermid syndrome may affect about 1 in 7,300 people
items.summary: An analysis suggests Phelan-McDermid syndrome, a genetic disorder linked to autism, may affect about 1 in 7,300 people, or more than 45,000 Americans, with many cases undiagnosed because genetic testing is often not performed.

items.title: Jim Copenhaver, shot at 2024 Trump rally in Butler, has died
items.summary: Jim Copenhaver, who was shot twice at a 2024 Trump campaign rally in Butler, has died. The gunman also killed another man and grazed Trump's ear.

items.title: CERN begins replacing LHC magnets for High-Luminosity upgrade
items.summary: CERN has started replacing key Large Hadron Collider magnets as part of its High-Luminosity upgrade. The new superconducting magnets produce fields about 40% stronger, allowing beams to be focused more tightly before collision.

items.title: Subduction zone off Vancouver Island observed tearing apart
items.summary: Scientists have observed a subduction zone off Vancouver Island breaking apart, suggesting such tectonic systems may end piece by piece rather than all at once.

items.title: Trump administration uses AI to review Medicare claims for seniors
items.summary: The Trump administration is using AI vendors to review and deny medical care claims for seniors. Critics say the vendors have an incentive to deny as many claims as possible.

items.title: Advocates say ICE detained at least four people at Concord Home Depot
items.summary: Advocates say at least four people were detained by ICE agents in a Concord Home Depot parking lot and are calling on Home Depot and Concord officials to respond.

items.title: Netanyahu addresses UN General Assembly and criticises opponents
items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used his UN General Assembly speech to criticise his critics, including Zohran Mamdani, before returning to Israel. The Assembly also heard from the Palestinian Authority and Yemen on Middle East crises.

items.title: Pentagon seeks $30.3 million for AI-powered lie detector
items.summary: A Department of Defense budget request seeks $30.3 million over five years for a program called Polygraph+ or Polygraph Next, focused on AI-based scoring algorithms for lie detection.

items.title: Switzerland votes on tightening its neutrality
items.summary: Swiss voters are deciding in a referendum whether to tighten the country's neutrality policy, a change that could affect its response to Russia and future conflicts.

items.title: Storm blows roofs off eight homes in Sangre Grande
items.summary: Heavy rain, lightning and strong winds in Sangre Grande blew the roofs off at least eight homes and brought down a communications tower.

items.title: Iran's president says country has "no trust" in the US
items.summary: Iran's president told a small group of journalists on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York that his country has no trust in the United States.

items.title: Hurricane Polo rapidly intensifies off Mexico's Pacific coast
items.summary: Hurricane Polo underwent explosive intensification off Mexico's Pacific coast, becoming one of the strongest storms recorded in the eastern Pacific basin.

items.title: Magnetic bacteria extend worm lifespan by 43%
items.summary: A magnet-producing bacterium extended the average lifespan of C. elegans worms by more than 43% and protected neurological and intestinal health, largely by suppressing ferroptosis, a form of iron-linked cell death.

items.title: White dwarf without a disk produces long-lasting shock wave
items.summary: Astronomers found a white dwarf with no detectable disk producing a shock wave that appears to have persisted for at least 1,000 years. Its magnetic field may be partly responsible, but the full mechanism is unexplained.

items.title: Venezuelan and Trinidad and Tobago leaders meet at UN General Assembly
items.summary: Leaders of Venezuela and Trinidad and Tobago met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.

items.title: Meteorite grains show strong magnetic field in early Solar System
items.summary: Grains from one of the oldest known meteorites indicate a strong magnetic field existed during the Solar System's first 200,000 years, suggesting magnetism worked with gravity to form the Sun and planets.

items.title: Scientists find backup pathway cells use to make cysteine
items.summary: Researchers found a mechanism that lets mammalian cells produce the amino acid cysteine even when pathways previously considered essential are disabled. The same mechanism may help cancer cells resist treatment.

items.title: California voters to choose next Secretary of State
items.summary: California voters will choose a new Secretary of State in November between two candidates with different approaches to running and protecting the state's elections.

items.title: California Supreme Court rules Riverside sheriff illegally seized 650,000 ballots
items.summary: In a unanimous ruling, the California Supreme Court said Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco broke the law when he seized more than 650,000 ballots from the November 2025 special election and ordered him to return them.

items.title: CDC opens state ordering for COVID-19 vaccines after delay
items.summary: The CDC opened ordering of COVID-19 vaccines for states after a delay it had previously attributed to procurement decisions that were not yet finalized.

items.title: San José leaders propose penalties for police misuse of Flock camera data
items.summary: San José officials proposed rules to tighten limits on unauthorized searches of Flock license plate camera data, which California law does not currently prohibit police from misusing.

items.title: F-Droid releases its biggest update in a decade
items.summary: The F-Droid open-source Android app store has been rebuilt with a new interface and smoother app installation.

items.title: Stanford removes banners after AI altered students' appearances in photo
items.summary: Stanford University removed campus banners after AI was used to alter the race and appearance of students in a promotional photo, drawing criticism from students. The university pledged a review.

items.title: New York sues to shut down Polymarket as illegal gambling
items.summary: New York asked a court to shut down Polymarket's operations in the state as illegal gambling, while the Trump administration seeks to override state gambling laws.

items.title: Study finds brain resolves conflicting visual signals through "consensus" mechanism
items.summary: Researchers found that matching signals between two visual brain areas persisted longer while conflicting signals quickly faded, pointing to a mechanism for resolving disagreements between brain regions.

items.title: Time crystals in a semiconductor shown to synchronize
items.summary: Researchers showed that multiple time crystals in a semiconductor can synchronize their oscillations through spin-polarized electrons, even when separated by up to 40 micrometers.

items.title: Study reveals new role of NUDT5 protein in 70-year-old leukemia drug's action
items.summary: Researchers found that removing the protein NUDT5 protected cells from a 70-year-old leukemia drug, although blocking the protein had little effect, pointing to a previously unknown cellular role.

items.title: Two new tiny snail species discovered in Montenegro
items.summary: Scientists described two new snail species in Montenegro, one living in Komarnica Canyon, where a proposed hydropower reservoir could destroy its habitat.

items.title: Uranus' moon Ariel may once have had a 100-mile-deep ocean
items.summary: A study suggests Uranus' moon Ariel may once have held a subsurface ocean more than 100 miles deep; with similar evidence from Miranda, the Uranian system could have multiple ocean worlds.

items.title: Hospital and insurer AI systems competing over claims are raising medical costs
items.summary: Hospitals and insurers are both deploying AI systems in billing and claims disputes, and the competition between them is pushing medical costs higher, according to The New York Times.

items.title: Danish study links rise in ADHD and autism diagnoses to broader identification
items.summary: A large Danish study found that children diagnosed with ADHD or autism today more closely resemble the general population than those diagnosed 10 years ago, suggesting rising rates partly reflect broader identification and changing diagnostic practices.

items.title: More REM sleep linked to lower risk of 83 diseases
items.summary: A study of more than 95,000 people found that those who spent more time in REM sleep had lower risks of 83 conditions, including dementia, heart failure and Parkinson's disease.

items.title: Rep. Delia Ramirez proposes ending US border surveillance tower program
items.summary: Illinois Democratic Representative Delia Ramirez announced plans to introduce legislation terminating the surveillance tower program along the US southern border, following an MIT Technology Review investigation.

items.title: Smart glasses recordings raise privacy concerns in India
items.summary: People in India are being recorded without their knowledge by smart glasses, including at a Delhi protest where footage was later posted to Instagram.
